canonical.rule: Improve the canonical runtime in place. Donor histories supply evidence, requirements, fixtures, and bounded behavior ports; they never supply a wholesale architecture.

candidates.title: Sanitize donor credential path and scan all preserved refs
candidates.decision: The provider credential was deleted, but tracked donor code and preserved history must be classified before any public archival branch or AI integration.
acceptance: Tracked donor tests read credentials only from ignored environment configuration.
All refs and dirty files are scanned without printing credential values.
Findings and remediation decisions are recorded in a public-safe report.
Pre-sanitization preservation bundles remain private.
candidates.supersededAction: Replace the tracked donor test credential literal with an environment-variable contract; retain pre-sanitization history only in private preservation.
candidates.nextAction: Perform the value-safe scan and prepare a narrowly scoped donor sanitation patch without publishing donor history.

candidates.title: Curate preserved donor work into reviewable evidence commits
candidates.decision: Preservation is complete, but review requires small thematic commits and asset classifications rather than giant dirty snapshots.
acceptance: Security, runtime, content, styling, PAO, documentation, and asset work are separated.
Generated output and likeness-dependent assets are classified before publication.
No curated commit changes the canonical runtime.
Every retained behavior points to a registry candidate or an archival rationale.
candidates.supersededAction: Freeze dirty donor worktrees as historical sources after their curated evidence commits are verified; do not develop features in them.
candidates.nextAction: Begin only after SEC-001 is verified.

candidates.title: Finish focused presentation ownership in the canonical runtime
candidates.decision: Reducing the remaining coordinator surface lowers the cost and ambiguity of every later mode or visual system.
acceptance: Extract only ownership demonstrated by the Season Zero journey.
No command bypasses RoundKernel or established domain owners.
Browser behavior and production journey evidence remain unchanged.
Each extraction adds a focused contract test.
candidates.supersededAction: Remove each extracted presentation responsibility from app.js or the renderer facade in the same verified change.
candidates.nextAction: Keep the Renderer facade stable and extract the next proven command/presentation workflow from the 651-line app coordinator without delaying original-IP and bilingual-content work.

candidates.title: Converge dialogue and controls into canonical component owners
candidates.canonicalOwner: semantic tokens plus one owned stylesheet per cabinet component
candidates.decision: Keep the canonical owned cascade, reject donor CSS wholesale, and carry useful arcade-control requirements through shared tactile tokens, a readable arena scoreboard, paper dialogue variants, and deterministic responsive fixtures.
acceptance: Dialogue uses available phone and tablet space without colliding with the host or control deck.
Primary, voice, host, and panel controls share tactile travel and focus behavior.
Scoreboard digits remain readable, animate without decorative strike-throughs, and use compact localized labels.
Generic host-study and language-help copy remains localized and accessible at icon-only widths.
Light and dark visual fixtures cover the supported viewport matrix.
CSS ownership and duplicate-selector gates remain clean.
candidates.supersededAction: Keep donor styling archived as visual research; do not reintroduce app-fixes.css, a legacy runtime sheet, or competing control and dialogue owners.
candidates.nextAction: Iterate through the deterministic visual matrix and component owners; mine donor versions only for documented behaviors that the canonical fixtures do not cover.

candidates.title: Classify fonts, host art, audio, backgrounds, and generated visuals
candidates.decision: Visual quality cannot converge while placeholders, historical references, generated work, and shippable originals are mixed together.
acceptance: Every production candidate records origin, rights status, intended use, dimensions, transparency, and derivative risk.
Reference-only likeness and audio assets are excluded from production manifests.
Duplicate and superseded assets receive an archive or deletion decision.
Canonical runtime references resolve to manifest-approved assets.
candidates.supersededAction: Move rejected, duplicate, reference-only, and likeness-dependent assets out of production manifests; delete only after preservation evidence is confirmed.
candidates.nextAction: Wait for curated asset inventories from OPS-001.

candidates.title: Port PAO as an isolated unlockable easter egg
candidates.decision: Preserve the desired nostalgic secret while preventing PAO state, rendering, or content from competing with the canonical game loop.
acceptance: PAO loads only after an explicit secret unlock.
Its storage namespace and lifecycle are isolated.
Editable content is rendered without unsafe HTML interpolation.
Entering and leaving PAO preserves the exact canonical session.
candidates.supersededAction: Keep the donor component hierarchy archived after its behavior is represented by the isolated canonical mode.
candidates.nextAction: Extract behavior requirements after donor curation; do not copy the donor component hierarchy.

candidates.title: Reinterpret full-board play through canonical episode contracts
candidates.decision: The board prototype contains useful selection rules, but its competing runtime ownership must not enter the canonical application.
acceptance: Board selection produces canonical episode clues rather than a parallel game state.
Reveal, answer, score, Study, media, translation, and resume use existing owners.
No incomplete mode is exposed as production-ready.
A complete board journey passes against the built artifact.
candidates.supersededAction: Archive the donor FullboardGameService after required selection rules are covered by canonical format-contract evidence.
candidates.nextAction: Write a format contract after CORE-001 reduces presentation coupling.

candidates.title: Introduce a provider-neutral HostDialogueGateway
candidates.canonicalOwner: server-side HostDialogueGateway plus deterministic HostPerformanceDirector fallback
candidates.decision: Gemini free tier may be an initial provider, but provider code, credentials, and generated dialogue cannot own canonical clues, scoring, or episode progression.
acceptance: No provider credential enters browser-delivered code, storage, logs, telemetry, or artifacts.
Provider outage, quota exhaustion, and invalid output fall back deterministically.
Generated output conforms to a versioned performance-command schema.
Canonical clue, answer, scoring, and episode facts remain immutable.
candidates.supersededAction: Archive browser-side provider orchestration and direct-DOM rewrite integrations; retain only provider-neutral requirements and safe fixtures.
candidates.nextAction: Defer implementation until the security gate and presentation ownership work are verified.

candidates.title: Mine historical sharding and validation work for missing fixtures
candidates.decision: The canonical pipeline is already stronger; historical code should contribute only uncovered validation cases and reproducible fixtures.
acceptance: Each imported fixture demonstrates a previously uncovered failure.
No second runtime question loader or shard format is introduced.
Archive content remains build-time research input rather than authored production truth.
candidates.supersededAction: Archive the historical loader and shard format after any genuinely missing fixtures are represented in canonical tests.
candidates.nextAction: Compare test cases after historical work is curated.
